profile.headline: Software Engineer II at Amazon
profile.summary: Enthusiastic engineer offering a bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering. An ambitious self-starter with dynamic interpersonal, analytical, and critical thinking skills. Looking for an opportunity to gain more software experience remotely.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Designed and built backend architecture for multiple applications, streamlining processes and reducing operation time from 30 to 5 minutes on a critical project.
•	Automated source code update process and set up pipelines for seamless algorithm updates, significantly improving productivity and efficiency.
•	Implemented a volatility detection algorithm, enhancing financial savings estimates’ accuracy and enabling data-driven decision-making.
•	Contributed to cost savings of $2.9M across 215 projects through efficient design and implementation strategies.
•	Garnered recognition from both teammates and superiors for surpassing expectations, embodying Amazon’s leadership principles, and delivering impactful outcomes.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer II
positions.description:
• Collaborated with a team to create GoDaddy's new payment method page using React. 
• Worked well in a team with a lot of pair programming. 
• Wrote unit tests to ensure efficiencies using mocha, jest, and test-library. 
• Created integration tests to ensure individual software modules operate correctly when connected, using cypress. 
• Provided assistance and guidance to other co-workers in the learning processes.

positions.title: Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
• Created a website application to display large amounts of data in various charts with React
and Redux.
• Lead team in creating a Snapchat replica using Meteor and React.
• Utilized an existing framework to create a Gmail replica with HTML and CSS.
• Maintained effective working relationships with team members to meet organizational goals.
• Participated in the design and creation of scalable software by writing clean, functional code
on the front and back end.

positions.title: Full-Stack Developer
positions.description: • Collaborated with a team remotely to build out a full-stack web application using React and Golang

positions.title: Freelance Full-Stack Developer
positions.description:
• Working remotely and collaborating with clients to discuss requirements, deadlines and completed work
• Developing creative solutions for websites and web applications from scratch, using a MERN tech stack
• Utilizing excellent organizational, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills to propel client projects to peak results

positions.title: Co-Founder and President
positions.description:
•	Leading a team of 5 remotely to develop websites for various clients
•	Delegate tasks and follow up on progression
•	Gather all project information from clients and regularly update clients on progression

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
•	Developed an algorithm using C# to solve a Travelling Salesman Problem to potentially improve productivity by at least 15% a week for up to 29 different items
•	Proposed and developed an application to simplify the process of cutting heat shrink and increased productivity by at least 50% a day using C# and MySQL
•	Created a label printer application using C# and Asp.Net
•	Developed a webform used to display and search a database using C#, Asp.Net, JavaScript, and MySQL
•	Automated processing scanned documents by creating an OCR application using C#

projects.title: SwampHacks, Hackathon
projects.description: Contributed to creating an application that pinpoints a person's location by displaying a 3D beacon on a camera, using Django, AWS, and Android Studio.

projects.title: HackRiddle, Hackathon
projects.description: Collaborated with a group of two to create two games that would respond to hand gestures using the Leap Motion SDK, Unity, and Python. The object of the first game was a man running trying to reach the furthest distance by avoiding objects by jumping and ducking. The jumping and ducking methods were based on someone's hand getting closer and further away from the Leap Motion. Moving on, the second game was rock paper scissors where the Leap Motion would obtain which choice someone made based on their hand gesture. This game was made multiplayer so two people could play against each other on different computers using a TCP server.

organizations.name: IEEE Workshop
organizations.description: Gain experience with hardware components using an Arduino.
